subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: What plugin-runtime breaker contract should OpenClaw support for repeated plugin hook/tool failures and crash-loop recovery?
rationale: The central design choices affect plugin API, persistent state, operator controls, fail-open versus fail-closed defaults, and upgrade behavior, which automation cannot choose safely from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design core breaker contract first
options.body: Specify the SQLite state model, hook/tool attribution fields, lifecycle states, status/reset CLI or doctor surface, and compatibility-safe defaults before queueing implementation.

options.title: Keep breaker logic plugin-owned
options.body: Close or narrow this issue to plugin-local breakers like Active Memory, leaving core to provide only generic health/status substrates.

options.title: Pursue process isolation instead
options.body: Redirect the work toward a larger worker/subprocess isolation architecture, accepting higher complexity and a broader compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker contract first
recommendation.body: Specify the SQLite state model, hook/tool attribution fields, lifecycle states, status/reset CLI or doctor surface, and compatibility-safe defaults before queueing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The previous public review and adjacent history make this the strongest cross-cutting routing candidate across plugin hooks, tools, locks, and health surfaces.
